knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: APIs that expose dtype or accumulation precision overrides may select different internal computation paths, causing numerically inconsistent results for low-precision inputs when explicit higher-precision computation is cast back.

risk_dimensions.shape: Large reduction dimensions or attention-like shapes that amplify accumulation differences.
risk_dimensions.dtype: Low-precision floating types such as float16 or bfloat16 and explicit higher-precision dtype arguments.
risk_dimensions.device: GPU/CUDA backend paths that may implement specialized low-precision kernels.
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Default dtype computation versus explicit dtype promotion followed by cast-back comparison.

failure_mechanism.layer: API Layer; Kernel Layer; Numerical Layer
failure_mechanism.description: The API dtype argument can expose different internal precision and accumulation paths. For low-precision inputs, the default path and explicit higher-precision path may use different accumulation orders or intermediate precisions, producing small numerical differences when cast back to the original dtype.

input_exploration: Vary low-precision dtypes such as float16 and bfloat16
Vary reduction dimensions and tensor shapes, including large and attention-like dimensions
Use value distributions with normal random, large magnitude, and small differences
constraint_awareness: Explicit dtype arguments may change internal accumulation or precision paths
Low-precision outputs require dtype-appropriate comparison tolerances
Backend-specific kernel behavior may differ across CPU and GPU
oracle_strategy: Compare default dtype path against explicit higher-precision dtype path cast back to the original dtype
Use max absolute difference or allclose with dtype-appropriate tolerances
Fail when numerical difference exceeds threshold

transferability.reason: The underlying risk applies to many APIs with dtype overrides or reduction/accumulation behavior, such as normalization, attention, loss, and reduction operations, where low-precision inputs and explicit higher-precision computation can expose path-dependent numerical differences.

important_considerations: Explore APIs with dtype or accumulation precision parameters
Vary low-precision dtypes and reduction shapes
Compare default low-precision path with explicit higher-precision path cast back to original dtype
Use tolerances appropriate for the reduced precision
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that systematically vary low-precision dtypes, shapes, and value distributions; compute the operation both with and without explicit higher-precision dtype; and compare outputs using numerical tolerances.
